questions.prompt: Why are Jordan and Morgan mentioned alongside Phelps and Biles?

To illustrate another successful route involving a broader sporting background.

vocabulary.meaning: 每有……也有……（此处为对照表达）

questions.prompt: Which scope makes the later-starter finding accurate?

questions.evidenceQuote: Another key finding from this study is that the success rate at the junior competition level is predicted by the earlier start age (the earlier, the more success), whereas the success rate at the adult competition level is predicted by the later start age. That is, in adult elite competition, the athletes who started the sport later in their lives were more successful than those who started early.

questions.prompt: What does 'translates to success' mean in the short-term statement?
questions.promptZh: 短期陈述中的 translates to success 是什么意思？
options: It means the passage is translated into another language.
It says every early result guarantees lifelong success.
It describes specialisation turning into success over the shorter time frame.
It denies that specialisation can have any immediate benefit.
optionsZh: 指文章被译成另一种语言。
说每个早期结果保证终生成功。
描写专攻在较短时段转化为成功。
否认专攻有任何即时益处。
analyses: A translate 在此为转化，不是语言翻译。
B short term 不能变成终生保证。
C 保留明确时间范围及转化比喻。
D 原句承认短期效果，后句才说长期未必回报。

vocabulary.meaning: 转化为；带来相应表现
vocabulary.context: 此处为短期效果表述，不是翻译动作，也不构成对每人的承诺。
vocabulary.example: Extra preparation often translates to a smoother presentation.

questions.evidenceQuote: In the short term, specialization translates to success. In the long term, however, it doesn’t always pay off. Indeed, this study found that a higher amount of youth-led play (e.g., pickup games) outside of an athlete’s primary sport was associated with higher performance among adult players. Surprisingly, a high number of main-sport practice hours was associated with lower performance among the world-class adult athletes.

questions.prompt: What does 'doesn't always pay off' say about long-term specialisation?

options: It does not invariably produce a worthwhile return.
It can never produce any return for anyone.
It always requires a financial payment to a coach.
It is guaranteed to outperform every other approach.

对任何人都绝无回报。
总要求向教练付钱。
保证胜过任何其他方法。
analyses: A not always 否定必然，不是否定一切可能。
B 把不总是强化成从不。
C pay off 是值得或有成效的习语，不是本句训练收费。
D 与长期未必回报相反。

vocabulary.meaning: 奏效；有回报；努力值得
vocabulary.context: 本句非偿清债务或实际支付费用。
vocabulary.example: The extra practice may pay off, but results can vary.

questions.evidenceQuote: In the short term, specialization translates to success. In the long term, however, it doesn’t always pay off. questions.prompt: Which reading preserves the finding about youth-led play?

Researchers assigned every child to stop coached practice permanently.
Adults with more childhood play were all identical in performance.

B 未报告全体儿童的随机干预或永久停训。
C associated 不建立全员结果相同。
D 保留 youth-led、outside、adult 与关联强度；e.g.pickupgames 为例而非仅此一种。

vocabulary.meaning: 由青少年自主主导的玩耍活动

questions.prompt: What does the shift to science contribute to the argument?
questions.promptZh: 转向科学领域为论证补充什么？
options: It explores whether a comparable specialisation pattern occurs in another domain.
It makes the sports findings automatically true of every scientist.
It says the same athletes also received the Nobel Prize.
It replaces all empirical findings with Nietzsche's quotation.
optionsZh: 考察另一领域是否出现可比较的专攻模式。
让体育发现自动适用于所有科学家。
说同一批运动员还获了诺奖。
用尼采引文替代所有实证发现。
analyses: A replicated in a completely different professional domain 引出另一研究。
B 跨域观察不等于无条件推广每个人。
C 人物群体不同，不能合并。

vocabulary.meaning: 领域；专业范围
vocabulary.context: 此处从体育到科学，不是网络域名或某人私有领土。

questions.evidenceQuote: Intriguingly, the early specialization effect was replicated in a completely different professional domain: science. Another study compared forty-eight German Nobel laureates in physics, chemistry, economics, and medicine/physiology with the winners of the Leibniz Prize, which is Germany’s highest national science award. Forty-two of the forty-eight Nobel laureates had engaged in multidisciplinary study or work experiences, suggesting a later specialization. The Leibniz Prize winners who did not win the Nobel Prize had earlier success than those who went on to be Nobel winners.

Only Nobel winners in literature and peace.

只有文学及和平诺奖得主。
所列学科四十八位德国诺奖得主与 Leibniz 奖得主。
同一批人随机获奖前后。

B 原句为物理、化学、经济及医学／生理学，不是这两类。
C another study compared 明确两组及四十八位诺奖者范围。

questions.evidenceQuote: For instance, Leibniz winners were more likely to have won a scholarship as students than Nobel laureates. My favorite finding: it took significantly longer for the eventual Nobel winners to earn full professorships than the Leibniz winners. So, Nobel laureates explored more diverse areas of study and made slower progress than Leibniz winners, but eventually reached the top without burning out.

questions.prompt: What does 'but eventually' contrast in the Nobel-laureate summary?

questions.prompt: What kind of support is supplied by the Nietzsche quotation?

A measured count of all young men's career decisions.
A guarantee that every person choosing early will fail.
A philosophical criticism illustrating distress about premature vocational choice.
optionsZh: 针对德国学生的新控制实验。
对所有青年职业决定的实测计数。
保证每位早选择者都失败。

questions.evidenceQuote: In the essay “Human, All Too Human” in his work Ecce Homo, Friedrich Nietzsche wrote about German specialization as follows: “I have discovered that a large number of young men experience the same distress: one antinatural step virtually compels the second. In Germany, the Reich—to speak unambiguously—all too many are condemned to choose vocations too early, and then to waste away under a burden they can no longer shake off.

questions.prompt: What is the effect of correcting 'a moment' to 'five or six hours'?

证明每位听者失去完全相同的时数。

questions.evidenceQuote: The story of William James Sidis presents another cautionary tale. He is often considered the smartest man to have ever lived. At age eight, he passed the Harvard Medical School’s anatomy exam, as well as the entrance exam to MIT. When Sidis was eleven years old, he gave a lecture on astrophysics at Harvard.

It means every prediction about his future was correct.

由新提供的全球统一 IQ 测验证明。
归于所有后来的诺奖得主，无一例外。
意味着对他未来的每项预测都正确。
analyses: A often considered 标记社会评价归属与频率，非作者新测定。
B 没有给全球测试或分数。
C 未有所有诺奖者一致评价的来源。

vocabulary.meaning: 常被认为；经常被视为

questions.evidenceQuote: The story of William James Sidis presents another cautionary tale. He is often considered the smartest man to have ever lived. At age eight, he passed the Harvard Medical School’s anatomy exam, as well as the entrance exam to MIT. When Sidis was eleven years old, he gave a lecture on astrophysics at Harvard.

questions.prompt: What was the status of the MIT professor's statement about Sidis?
questions.promptZh: MIT 教授对 Sidis 的话属于什么性质？
options: A report that the predicted career had already been completed.
A future prediction voiced by an attendee at the lecture.
The result of the later Nobel-versus-Leibniz comparison.
A direct statement by Sidis about his own final achievements.
optionsZh: 报告所预测职业已全部实现。
讲座在场者作出的未来预测。
后来诺奖与 Leibniz 比较的结果。
Sidis 对自己最终成就的直接陈述。
analyses: A would be 表从过去看未来，不是已完成成就。
B An MIT physics professor in attendance...remarked 清楚标说话人及预测。

questions.prompt: What does 'But the professor's prediction was wrong' contrast?
questions.promptZh: But the professor's prediction was wrong 对照什么？

The professor never attending any lecture.
The idea that every early achievement was fabricated.
An optimistic forecast and the later outcome described as burnout.

每项早期成就都是编造的主张。
乐观预言与后来所述倦怠结局。

vocabulary.meaning: 预测；对尚未发生之事的判断

questions.promptZh: Sidis 叙述中的 burned out 是什么意思？
options: He was literally injured by a fire at the lecture.
He lost the ability to remember any fact.
He became exhausted or lost the drive to continue, as the book describes.
He fulfilled every optimistic career prediction.

questions.prompt: What makes the schedule especially demanding for Ohtani in the book's account?
questions.promptZh: 按本书叙述，什么让 Ohtani 的赛程尤其吃力？
options: He pitches in most games and hits only about once a week.
He hits in most games and also pitches at least weekly.
He both hits and pitches in every game without any exceptions.
His schedule excludes postseason games and consists only of spring training.
optionsZh: 他多数比赛投球，仅约每周打击一次。
他多数比赛打击，并至少每周投球一次。
他每场都打击与投球，没有任何例外。

questions.evidenceQuote: The Major League Baseball season is long and grueling, consisting of 33 spring training games, 162 regular season games, and up to 22 postseason games—a total of 217 games! This schedule is especially demanding for Shohei Ohtani of the Dodgers, as he hits in most games and pitches at least once a week. He has grit and confidence. But he also has playfulness.

questions.prompt: Which two qualities are named before the contrast about playfulness?
questions.promptZh: 提到玩心的转折前，点名哪两种品质？
options: Grit and confidence.
Grit and playfulness.
Confidence and playfulness.
Talent and luck.
optionsZh: 坚毅与自信。
坚毅与玩心。
自信与玩心。
天赋与运气。
analyses: A He has grit and confidence 是转折前的完整两项。
B playfulness 在后一句被 also 增补，不能移到此前两项中。
C 保留 confidence 却用后句玩心替代 grit，混淆顺序。

questions.prompt: Which scope does the 3-for-24 statistic describe?

Every game in the current season as newly checked data.
His start to the 2022 season as a hitter, as reported by the book.

刚核验的当前赛季每场比赛。
